name: DGET
description: DGET extracts a single value from a specified field of the database record that matches the given criteria. It returns #NUM! if more than one record matches and #VALUE! if none match.
tldr: Pulls one value from a database column when exactly one row meets the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to extract from, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and exactly one condition row that uniquely identifies a single record.

basicExample.description: Extract the Yield of the single cherry tree
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:A10 (Tree=Cherry) matches exactly one record, so DGET returns its Yield of 9.

advancedExamples.title: Multiple matches cause #NUM!
advancedExamples.scenario: Criteria that matches more than one row
advancedExamples.description: Using Tree=Apple, Height>10 matches two rows, which is ambiguous for a single-value extract.
advancedExamples.explanation: DGET found more than one matching record, so it returns #NUM! because it cannot choose one.

advancedExamples.title: No match causes #VALUE!
advancedExamples.description: Using Tree=Banana, which does not exist in the database.
advancedExamples.explanation: No record satisfied the criteria, so DGET returns #VALUE!.

howItWorks: DGET filters the database to rows matching the criteria and then checks how many records remain. If exactly one remains, it returns the value from the specified field. If zero remain it returns #VALUE!; if two or more remain it returns #NUM!.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up a unique criteria
howToSteps.text: Create a criteria range that matches exactly one record, e.g. A9:A10 with Tree and Cherry.

limitations: Requires the criteria to match exactly one record; it is not meant for aggregating multiple rows.
Returns #NUM! when more than one record matches and #VALUE! when none match.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: More than one record satisfied the criteria, so the result is ambiguous.
commonErrors.fix: Tighten the criteria so only one record matches, or use DSUM/DMAX/etc. for aggregates.
Verify the criteria values and header spelling match the database.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DGET works identically in Google Sheets, including the same #NUM! and #VALUE! behavior.

faq.question: Why did DGET return #NUM!?
faq.answer: Because more than one record matched your criteria. DGET can only return a value when exactly one record matches.

faq.question: Why did DGET return #VALUE!?
faq.answer: Because no record matched your criteria at all.

faq.question: How do I get a value when several rows match?
faq.answer: Use an aggregate D-function such as DSUM, DMAX, or DAVERAGE instead of DGET.
